title: sudo: Run as administrator
body: "sudo" is a term used in Linux and Ubuntu to run commands with administrative privileges.
detail: Since regular users cannot freely modify system-wide settings or specific folders, they use "sudo" to run commands with higher privileges when necessary. However, because these privileges are so powerful, a single mistake could corrupt system files. When you see `sudo` while running code or installing a package, you should verify whether the task truly requires administrative privileges and what files or settings it will modify. Using it habitually can be dangerous. sudo is used to run installations or system configurations that cannot be performed with standard user privileges, by executing them with administrative privileges. title: Environment Variables: Settings Outside the Code
body: Environment variables are configuration values supplied from outside the source code at runtime.
detail: The same code can use different API endpoints or modes on a development PC and a server, and API keys do not have to be written directly in the source. Python reads them by name with calls such as `os.getenv('NAME')` or `os.environ['NAME']`. Environment-variable values are strings by default, so numbers and booleans need conversion and validation. Check the variable name, where it is set, what happens when it is missing, and whether it can appear in logs or the UI. Using an environment variable does not automatically make a secret secure. `os.getenv('RUN_LIMIT', '100')` returns the string `'100'` when the variable is missing. Code that needs a number must convert it, for example with `int(...)`. A local `.env` file can be loaded into environment variables, but a file containing real secrets is normally excluded from Git. A deployed service may use the hosting platform's secret settings instead.

body: Harvest is the data collection phase. It retrieves raw data from sources such as web pages, APIs, files, and RSS feeds, and either stores it or passes it on to the next processing stage. title: Curation: The process of selecting what is important
body: Curation is the process of selecting what is important from a large number of candidates. Once data is collected, not every item is equally useful. Duplicate items, outdated items, low-quality items, and items that do not fit the topic must be filtered out. In Python code, this process typically involves calculating scores, sorting, filtering, and selecting the top N items. When reading code, you must verify the criteria used to decide what to keep and what to discard. It is helpful to view this as a selection stage that determines the quality of the results.

title: Cache: Temporarily stores frequently used results
body: Caching is a method of temporarily storing frequently used results. Recalculating the same request from scratch or re-making the API call every time takes a long time and increases costs. Therefore, previous results are stored so that when the same request is received, it can be returned quickly. In web apps, file caching, API response caching, and browser caching can all be used. When reading code, while caching helps improve speed and reduce costs, you must also consider the risk of outdated results remaining.
